title: Reference
description: One source record: a website, product, image, printed work, or physical object. Rich-text fields accept [text](url), [text](ref:id), [text](style:id), [text](page:name), **bold**, *emphasis*, and `code`.

titleBreak.description: Optional title with a single line break marked by |, for the page heading.

lede.description: Rich text. One sentence on the reference page under the title.

summary.description: Rich text. One sentence for index rows.

archive.description: A Wayback Machine or other archive copy of the source.

made.description: When the work was made or published, as stated by the source. Example: 1957, c. 1985, 2011-2013.

note.description: Rich text. The basis for the level.

reviewed.description: Date of the last review attempt.

note.description: Rich text. Why this reference belongs to this style.

basis.description: curator: a person placed it. agent: an agent proposed it and no person has reviewed it.

qualifier.description: Short text shown after the style link, for example 'user-selected seed'.

notice.description: Rich text. A warning shown near the top, for example why a source is pending.

observed.description: Visual traits supported by the evidence.

related.description: Rich text shown at the end of the page.

display.description: diagram: small drawing shown whole with padding.

caption.description: Rich text. What the image shows and where it comes from.

original.description: Direct URL of the original image file.

tier.description: A: open license, stored. C: own capture of a third-party work. D: link and metadata only.

license.description: An SPDX-style identifier such as CC0-1.0, the phrase 'public domain', or 'unverified'.

statement.description: Rich text. The rights statement from the source, or a note.

identifiers.description: External IDs: wikidata, met, aic, cleveland, smithsonian, and others.
